author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text:
From Ralph Waldo Emerson's essay Self-Reliance.

Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.

Society everywhere is in conspiracy against the manhood of every one of its members.

Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.

Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
title: Self-Reliance

author: Plato, translated by Benjamin Jowett
text:
From Plato's Apology, translated by Benjamin Jowett.

I know that I have no wisdom, small or great.

The unexamined life is not worth living.

Wherefore, O judges, be of good cheer about death, and know of a certainty, that no evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
title: Apology

author: James Madison
text:
From Federalist No. 10 by James Madison.

Liberty is to faction what air is to fire, an aliment without which it instantly expires.

The latent causes of faction are thus sown in the nature of man.

Enlightened statesmen will not always be at the helm.
title: Federalist No. 10
